title: Verifier-integrated LLM intent→configuration pipeline: an artifact-grounded paired evaluation and lessons from a ceiling effect
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired experiment (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001) that tested whether integrating an automated network verifier (block-on-violation) into an LLM intent→configuration pipeline reduces unsafe enactments. Using gpt-5-mini and a shared-initial generation policy across 150 paired intents (300 episodes), baseline (LLM-only) and guarded (LLM+verifier-block) pipelines produced identical generated candidates that the deterministic validator accepted in all episodes (n11=150; n10=n01=n00=0). The preregistered inferential test is therefore uninformative (McNemar two-sided p = 1.0); paired-bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0,0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). We present the full artifact-backed execution and scoring traces (representative file paths and SHA256 hashes cited inline), diagnose why a ceiling effect occurred (shared-initial policy + validator acceptance predicates), correct a preregistration–execution mismatch (the preregistered rollback hypothesis H2 was not testable/executed), and give artifact-grounded recommendations (adversarial/stateful task banks, independent per-condition generation, multi-model/multi-verifier matrices) to expose verifier-sensitive failure modes. All raw transcripts, validator traces, scoring JSONs, analysis scripts, and SHA256 hashes are archived and referenced.

sections.introduction: LLM-driven intent-to-configuration translation promises operational efficiency for NetOps but raises safety and reliability concerns: incorrect configurations can disrupt reachability, violate policy, or trigger outages. A common mitigation is a generate→validate→(repair|block|rollback) architecture pairing a generative LLM with an automated verifier. We preregistered CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001 to test the confirmatory hypothesis H1 that an LLM+verifier (block-on-violation) reduces per-task unsafe-enactment rates relative to an LLM-only pipeline in a paired design. A secondary preregistered hypothesis (H2) planned to test whether verifier-detected violations, when routed to an automated rollback procedure, reduce service-impact. Contributions: (1) a fully machine-readable preregistration and deterministic execution manifest; (2) a complete artifact-backed paired run including per-episode validator/scorer traces and SHA256 manifests; (3) a diagnosis of a deterministic ceiling effect that prevented inferential conclusions and prescriptive, artifact-grounded recommendations for future verifier evaluation.
sections.related_work: Work on LLMs for NetOps emphasizes verifier- and tool-assisted pipelines and workload-centered evaluation rather than standalone QA metrics (selected verified items: OpenAlex W7114889968, W7155247165, W7161354925; Nguyen et al., 2024 doi:10.1002/nem.2313). The generate–validate–repair literature and RAG/verification surveys motivate our paired workflow and preregistration. Where prior studies show verifier value, they typically (i) use adversarial or stateful tasks that exercise reachability/timing invariants, (ii) evaluate multiple verifiers or richer reachability checks, or (iii) allow independent generation per condition. Our experiment purposefully recorded all artifacts so others can replay, audit, and extend the exact pipeline.
sections.methodology: Preregistration: CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001 (preregistration SHA256 = 66fbf2c56649115c66412326fcc739ebacced84ec2df3fca796f4e7eac4a9b04). Design: paired binary episodes (150 tasks, each executed under baseline and guarded conditions → 300 episodes). Strata: intents synthesized across three ambiguity levels (benign / ambiguous / partially-specified). Model and generation policy: gpt-5-mini with a shared_initial_candidate policy (one initial generation call per task; at most one repair call permitted); model_configuration.json SHA256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa. Verifier/scorer: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 recorded per-episode in execution/scoring/*.json. Primary estimand: per-task unsafe-enactment rate difference (LLM-only minus LLM+verifier-block). Definition used in analysis (binary unsafe enactment): an enactment is labeled unsafe iff the validator marks valid==false or violation_count > 0 in the episode scoring JSON. This mapping is deterministic and implemented in the scoring scripts archived with the run. Analysis: paired McNemar two-sided test (primary), complemented by paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Contamination and exclusions: automatic rules (non-RFC1918 exclusion, public-org name regex, exact-match fingerprinting) were enforced; results are logged (analysis/contamination_summary.csv). Execution manifest reports completed_episode_count=300, model_calls_used=150, failed_episode_count=0.
sections.results: Execution and scoring (artifact-backed): 150 paired tasks (300 episodes), model_calls_used = 150 (one per task). Scoring JSONs show validator acceptance for every episode: baseline valid-configurations = 150/150 (100.0%); guarded valid-configurations = 150/150 (100.0%). Paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv sha256 = c2ba9cdb5d0938eae910129ba511eadf309319e6e05b36d9e3b4860032deb80e) is: n11=150, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Deterministic reconciliation and provider-call audit pass: execution manifest reports no failed provider calls and full accounting (see execution manifest and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). Representative archived artifacts (minimal reproducibility set below) fully substantiate these counts and per-episode validator fields (violation_count, valid, difficulty.pattern, required_command_count).
sections.discussion: Why the results are uninformative (artifact-grounded diagnosis). Two deterministic facts—both recorded in archived artifacts—explain the degenerate inferential outcome: (A) identical shared-initial outputs across conditions. For every confirmatory task the baseline and guarded response files are byte-identical (per-response SHA256s match across conditions; representative response execution/responses/task-000001-guarded.txt sha256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080). Because the guarded pipeline received the same candidate, it had nothing new to block. (B) the deterministic validator accepted every candidate: scoring JSONs show violation_count == 0 and valid == true for all episodes (representative scoring JSON execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json sha256 = 974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe61616d6b471cf2e6bfbd5e5cbabe82701957cbeea14). Consequence: the preregistered H1 comparison could not reveal verifier benefit (no discordant pairs). The preregistered H2 (rollback success/time-to-rollback) was not testable because no verifier-detected violations occurred and the rollback branch was never invoked; the absence of rollback events is artifact-backed (no rollback traces in scoring JSONs or execution manifest). Statistical note: McNemar p = 1.0 and bootstrap CI = [0.0,0.0] are degenerate outputs when n10 = n01 = 0; these values are not evidence of equivalence or of verifier irrelevance but rather reflect a design-driven ceiling. Validator construct limitations: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces command-parsing, required_command_count, and configured predicate checks (examples of difficulty.pattern observed in the corpus: "make_before_break_uplink_switchover" and "paired_link_atomic_mtu_change"); it does not, in this execution, exercise richer emulated reachability/timing invariants (these gaps are visible in the scorer fields recorded in each scoring JSON). Prescriptions (artifact-grounded): (1) use independent per-condition generation or controlled perturbations so baseline and guarded pipelines can produce different candidates; (2) design adversarial/stateful tasks that exercise validator-recorded temporal/cross-command invariants (difficulty.pattern fields are a useful target); (3) include multi-verifier matrices (e.g., add a reachability SMT or header-space verifier) to expose verifier-specific discordance; (4) instrument canary reachability tests in the emulation so rollback hypotheses become testable. All proposals are motivated by fields and examples present in the archived scoring JSONs and reconciliation logs.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired study comparing an LLM-only pipeline against an LLM+verifier-block pipeline. In the executed regime (gpt-5-mini, shared_initial generation, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, 150 paired tasks), every generated candidate satisfied the validator in both conditions (n11=150), producing a deterministic ceiling that rendered the preregistered confirmatory comparisons uninformative (McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap CI = [0.0,0.0]). The scientific value is the artifact-backed lesson: benchmark, generation policy, and validator must be co-designed to create discordant outcomes that let a verifier's value be measured. We release the full artifact bundle (preregistration, execution manifest, per-episode scoring JSONs, response files, and analysis scripts with SHA256 hashes) so follow-up work can replay, adversarialize, and instrument the pipeline to reveal verifier-sensitive failure modes.

disclosure_statement: Autonomy and human boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad topic family and provided the initial master prompt and autonomy constraints before the autonomy lock. After the lock the AI autonomously performed the literature review, research-question selection, machine-readable preregistration (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001; preregistration SHA256 = 66fbf2c56649115c66412326fcc739ebacced84ec2df3fca796f4e7eac4a9b04), experiment implementation, deterministic execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer-review checks, and revision. Models, prompts, and orchestration: the executed pipeline used a single hosted model recorded as gpt-5-mini (model_configuration.json sha256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa) under adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Generation policy: shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation call per task; at most one repair call), frozen per preregistration. Verifier and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 was the scorer/verifier used; per-episode validator traces (execution/scoring/*.json) record acceptance predicates (required_command_count, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count, valid). Execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation: the run executed 300 episodes (150 paired tasks), used 150 model calls, and completed with zero failed episodes (execution manifest; provider-call audit shows 150 completed hosted-model call events). Preregistration vs execution: the preregistration included a secondary hypothesis H2 about verifier-triggered automated rollback; in the confirmatory execution H2 was not testable and effectively unexecuted because no verifier-detected violations occurred and the rollback branch was never invoked. This deviation is disclosed here and is artifact-backed (no rollback events recorded in scoring JSONs or execution manifest). Reproducibility artifacts: representative artifacts and SHA256 hashes (selected) — preregistration JSON SHA256 = 66fbf2c5..., model_configuration.json SHA256 = 1acce925..., representative scoring JSON execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA256 = 974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe6..., response file execution/responses/task-000001-guarded.txt SHA256 = 8f38c8be...; paired contingency table analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA256 = c2ba9cdb...; contamination summary analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA256 = 389227f0.... All raw outputs, provider-call traces, scoring JSONs, analysis scripts, and full SHA256 manifest are archived in the execution bundle. Human editing: no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock; manuscript revisions responding to peer review were implemented autonomously using the archived artifacts. Restarts and deviations: only automated retries allowed by the preregistered retry policy were used; no manual experimental reruns aimed at improving outcomes were performed. Limitations: synthetic/emulated benchmark, single-model and single-validator scope, validator acceptance predicates constrain construct validity; these are discussed explicitly in the manuscript's Limitations section.
limitations: Ceiling effect: both pipelines produced validator-acceptable configurations in all 150 confirmatory tasks, preventing the preregistered inferential comparison from being informative.
Synthetic/emulated benchmark: CNSM-AI-NetOps-Intent-Bench-v1 is synthetic and may not exercise live timing/transient invariants present in production NetOps.
Single-model and single-validator scope: experiments used only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; results do not generalize across LLM or verifier families.

Validator predicates: the validator enforced syntactic/semantic predicates recorded in scoring JSONs (e.g., required_command_count, violation_count==0); different verifier designs (reachability SMT, header-space checks) may produce different rejection/rollback behavior.
Rollback hypothesis untested: the preregistered H2 (automated rollback performance) was not testable because the rollback branch was never invoked; this is disclosed and artifact-backed.
Contamination detection limits: automatic detectors flagged zero contaminated tasks, but heuristic scans cannot eliminate subtle training-data leakage.
